<DIV style="font-family: Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif">

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Since July&nbsp;2005, Vale is considered investment grade. Currently, Vale has the following credit
risk ratings: BBB&#043; (Standard &#038; Poor&#146;s), Baa2 (Moody&#146;s), BBB high (Dominion Bond Ratings) e BBB&#043;
(Fitch).
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<B>i. relevant loan and financing contracts</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The short term debt consists principally of financing for export (trade financing<I>) </I>and import
expressed in US dollars, with financial institutions. On December&nbsp;31<SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">st</SUP>, 2010 the short
term debt was R$1,144&nbsp;billion, as compared to R$646&nbsp;million and R$1,088&nbsp;billion in 2009 and 2008,
respectively.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The most important categories of the long term debt are presented below. The values presented
include the short term portion of the long term debt and exclude the accumulated costs.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Loans and financing expressed in US dollar (R$ 10.7&nbsp;billion, R$14.5&nbsp;billion and R$16.3
billion on 31</I><SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top"><I>th</I></SUP><I> of December&nbsp;2010, 2009 e 2008, respectively). These loans include credit
facilities for export, financing of import of the export credit agencies and loans from commercial
banks and multilateral organizations. The main credit facility is a prepayment of export, linked to
future exports, originally in the amount of US$6.0&nbsp;billion (equivalent to R$10.4&nbsp;billion), captured
as part of the refinancing of the debt for the acquisition of Inco. On December&nbsp;31</I><SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top"><I>st</I></SUP><I>,
2010, the outstanding balance was US$2.7&nbsp;billion (equivalent to R$4.4&nbsp;billion)</I>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Fixed income papers expressed in US dollars (R$17.1&nbsp;billion, R$12.9&nbsp;billion and R$15.2&nbsp;billion
on December&nbsp;31</I><SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top"><I>st</I></SUP><I>, 2010, 2009 e 2008, respectively). Vale issued several debt instruments
in the capitals market through its wholly owned subsidiary Vale Overseas in the total amount of
US$9.1&nbsp;billion (equivalent to R$15.2&nbsp;billion). The subsidiary Vale Canada issued debt instruments
in the amount of US$1.1&nbsp;billion (equivalent to R$1.9&nbsp;billion).</I>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Fixed income papers in euros (R$1.7&nbsp;billion on 31 December&nbsp;2010). Vale issued a debt
instrument in the capitals market in the total amount of Euros 750&nbsp;million (equivalent to R$1.7
billion).</I>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Instruments expressed in US dollars guaranteed by receivables of future exports (R$0.3&nbsp;billion
and R$0.5&nbsp;billion on December&nbsp;31</I><SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top"><I>st</I></SUP><I>, 2009 and 2008, respectively). In December&nbsp;2009, we
had a securitization program originally in the amount of US$400&nbsp;million based on existing and
future accounts receivable related to export of iron ore and pellets to customers in Europe, Asia
and the USA. On 15 January&nbsp;2010, Vale liquidated in advance the remaining balance of the
securitization program.</I>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Non-convertible debentures expressed in reais (R$4.7&nbsp;billion, R$6.0&nbsp;billion and R$6.0&nbsp;billion
on December&nbsp;31</I><SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top"><I>st</I></SUP><I>, 2010, 2009 and 2008, respectively). In November&nbsp;2006, we issue non
convertible debentures in the value of approximately US$3.2&nbsp;billion (equivalent to R$5.5&nbsp;billion),
in two series, with maturities of four and seven years. The first series, of US$862&nbsp;million
(equivalent to R$1.5&nbsp;billion), fell due in 2010, with interest of 101.75% of the accrued variation
of the interest rate of the CDI (interbank deposit certificate). The second series, of US$2.3
billion (equivalent to R$4.0&nbsp;billion), with maturity on 2013 has interest of variation of the CDI
plus 0.25% per year.</I>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Perpetual instruments (R$0.1&nbsp;billion, R$0.1&nbsp;billion and R$0.2&nbsp;billion on December
31</I><SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top"><I>st</I></SUP><I>, 2010, 2009 and 2008, respectively). We issued perpetual instruments which are
negotiable for 48.0&nbsp;billion preferred shares of Minera&#231;&#227;o Rio do Norte S.A (MRN). The interest is
paid on the instruments in a value equal to the dividends paid to the underlying preferred shares.</I>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<B>ii. other long-term relationships with financial institutions</B>
</DIV>





<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->&nbsp;<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>

<!-- PAGEBREAK -->
<P><HR noshade><P>
<H5 align="left" style="page-break-before:always"><A HREF="#H04912tocpage">Table of Contents</A></H5><P>

<DIV style="font-family: Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif">



<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Vale and its associated and subsidiary companies have a commercial relationship in the normal
course of their business with some of the main financial institutions of the country, according to
the usual practices of the financial market.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Other debts totaled R$7.8&nbsp;billion, R$7.2&nbsp;billion and R$5.4&nbsp;billion on December&nbsp;31<SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">st</SUP>,
2010, 2009 and 2008, respectively. We have several loans contracted in Brazil, especially with
BNDES and some Brazilian private banks, in addition to loans and financing in other currencies.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<B>iii. degree of subordination among debts</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The total outstanding balance was not guaranteed by receivables in 2010, 4% of the total
outstanding balance was guaranteed by receivables in 2009 and 3% in 2008.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<B>iv. eventual restrictions imposed on the issuer especially, in relation to limits of
indebtedness and contracting of new debts, to the distribution of dividends, to the disposal of
assets, to the issue of new securities and to the disposal of corporate control</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Some of the long term financial instruments contain obligations related to financial indicators.
The main indicators re debt on shareholders&#146; equity, debt on Earnings Before Interest Tax,
Depreciation and Amortization (EBITDA)&nbsp;and interest coverage. Vale is in conformity with the levels
required for the indicators. We believe that the current clauses shall not significantly restrict
the capacity to contract new debts to meet capital needs. Additionally, none of the clauses
restricts directly our capacity to distribute dividends or interest on net current assets.
</DIV>

<P><HR noshade><P>
<H5 align="left" style="page-break-before:always"><A HREF="#H04912tocpage">Table of Contents</A></H5><P>

<DIV style="font-family: Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif">




<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><B><I>Revenues</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The net operating revenue reached R$83.225&nbsp;billion in 2010 versus R$ 48.496&nbsp;billion in 2009, an
increase of 71.6%.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">In 2010, the increase in revenue was due basically to the largest volume sold and to the increase
in prices of the principal products sold by the Company, which contributed to an increase in
revenue of R$ 7.366&nbsp;billion and R$ 28.167&nbsp;billion, respectively, compared with 2009.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The expansion in revenue was determined mainly by higher prices of iron ore, R$ 17.953&nbsp;billion,
pellets R$6.880&nbsp;billion, and by the purchase of Vale Fosfatados and Vale Fertilizantes, which
contributed with revenue of R$ 2.419&nbsp;billion.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Iron ore</I>
</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Revenues from iron ore sales increased by 80%, from R$ 25.234&nbsp;billion in 2009 to R$ 45.419&nbsp;billion
in 2010, due to a 71.1% increase in the average sale price and an 8.8% in volumes sold. The
increase in prices reflects strong demand.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Pellets</I>
</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Revenues from pellet shipments increased 266% from R$ 3.887&nbsp;billion in 2009 to R$ 14.227&nbsp;billion in
2010 due to a 177.8% variation in average sales prices and an 89.3% increase of volumes sold.
Higher prices are explained by the same methodology applied in iron ore, while higher volumes are
explained by the increased use of plants due to market recovery.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Manganese ore</I>
</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Revenues from manganese ore increased 66.5%, from de R$ 275&nbsp;million in 2009 to R$ 458&nbsp;million in
2009 due to prices positive variation of 53.1% as a result of the impact of global economic
conditions and to the increase in volumes sold of 13.5% due to demand recovery.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Ferroalloys</I>
</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Revenues from ferroalloys sales increased 57.4%, from R$ 693&nbsp;billion in 2010 to R$ 1.091&nbsp;billion in
2009, due to a 58.5% increase in volumes sold due to the recovery of steel industry. The alloys
average price remained stable by the variation of mix of alloys sold.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Nickel and other products</I>
</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Revenues from this segment increased by 4.3%, from R$ 7.868&nbsp;billion in 2009 to R$ 8.204&nbsp;billion in
2010, mainly due to the following factors:
</DIV>



<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-left: 4%"><B>&#149;</B> Revenues from nickel sales increased 3.7%, from R$ 6.457&nbsp;billion in 2010 to R$ 6.698
billion in 2009, due to a 26.4% increase in average nickel prices. Nickel volume sold
declined by 22.8% in 2009 due to the shutdown of our Sudbury and Voisey Bay operations as a
result of labor strikes beginning in the second half of 2009; and
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-left: 4%"><B>&#149;</B> Revenue from copper sales increased 28% from R$ 903&nbsp;million in 2009 to R$ 1.156&nbsp;billion
in 2010, primarily due to an increase of 33.8% in average selling prices in part offset by
a 5.7% drop in volumes sold due to the shutdowns described above.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Copper concentrate</I>
</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Revenues from copper concentrate sales increased 23.3%, from R$ 1.329&nbsp;billion in 2010 to R$ 1.638
billion in 2009, due to a 25.8% increase in average sale prices.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Aluminum</I>
</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Revenues from our aluminum business increased 10.6%, from R$ 4.217&nbsp;billion in 2009 to R$ 4.663
billion in 2010 mainly due to LME price variation.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Potash</I>
</DIV>

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->&nbsp;<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>

<!-- PAGEBREAK -->
<P><HR noshade><P>
<H5 align="left" style="page-break-before:always"><A HREF="#H04912tocpage">Table of Contents</A></H5><P>

<DIV style="font-family: Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif">
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Revenues from potash sales decreased 39.3%, from R$ 810&nbsp;billion in 2009 to R$ 492&nbsp;million in 2010,
due to significant drops in sales volumes, of 13.9%, explained by recuperation of internal
inventory and by reduction of average prices in 25,3%.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Phosphate</I>
</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Sales revenue is attributed to the acquisition of Vale Fosfatados (formerly known as Bunge
Participa&#231;&#245;es e Investimentos S.A.) and Vale Fertilizantes (formerly known as Fosfertil).
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Nitrogen</I>
</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Sales revenue is attributed to the acquisition of Vale Fosfatados and Vale Fertilizantes.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Logistics services</I>
</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Revenue from logistics services increased 14%, from R$ 2.838&nbsp;billion in 2009 to R$ 3.236
billion in 2010 mainly due to the mix of products transported.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Other products and services</I>
</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Revenues from other products and services increased from R$ 1.190&nbsp;billion in 2009 to R$ 1.664
billion in 2010. This occurred mainly because of higher revenues from steel products.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><I>Services Costs and Expenses</I>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Costs related to services and goods sold by Vale are detailed below:
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><I>Comments on Cost by Type of Product</I>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Our total cost of goods sold increased from R$ 27.750&nbsp;billion in 2009 to R$ 33.756&nbsp;billion in 2010,
a 21.6% increase, due to higher volumes sold. The following were the main factors that contributed
to this variation:
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<B>&#149;</B> Outsourced services. Outsourced services costs increased by 8.6% in 2010, from R$ 4.274
billion in 2009 to R$ 4.640&nbsp;billion in 2010, due to higher volumes sold.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<B>&#149;</B> Materials costs. Materials costs increased by 2.2% in 2010, from R$ 5.943&nbsp;billion in 2009 to
R$ 6.071&nbsp;billion in 2010, reflecting the increase in demand. In 2009 there was the anticipation of
maintenance reflecting in the consumption of inputs in this period.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<B>&#149;</B> Costs of energy and fuels. Energy costs decreased by 2.9% in 2010, from R$ 6.034&nbsp;billion in
2009 to R$ 5.858&nbsp;billion in 2010. This increase reflected higher volumes sold and prices.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<B>&#149;</B> Staff costs. Staff costs decreased 3.8%, from R$ 4.077&nbsp;billion in 2009 to R$ 3.921&nbsp;billion
in 2010, reflecting the temporary interruption occurred in nickel, impacting on the reduction
volumes sold, partially offset by an adjustment of 7% in payroll in Brazil.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<B>&#149;</B> Acquisition of products. The cost of products purchased from third parties increased by
56.1%, from R$ 1.219&nbsp;billion in 2009 to R$ 1.903&nbsp;billion in 2010 mainly due to higher volumes sold
of pellets.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<B>&#149;</B> Depreciation and depletion. The cost of depreciation and depletion increased 5.9%, from R$
4.642&nbsp;billion in 2009 to R$ 4.916&nbsp;billion in 2010. Part of the increase due to acquisition of
fertilizer companies.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<B>&#149;</B> Other costs. Increased 110.8% in 2010, from R$ 3.058&nbsp;billion in 2009 to R$ 6.447&nbsp;billion in
2010, mainly due to allocation of fertilizer costs of in this nature &#151; Vale Fosfatados and Vale
Fertilizantes.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Selling, general and administrative expenses</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Selling, general and administrative expenses increased by 36.3%, from R$ 2.347&nbsp;billion in 2009 to
R$ 3.201&nbsp;billion in 2010. The increase was explained by increased expenses in services, advertising
and personnel related to increased level of product commercialization.
</DIV>

1.567&nbsp;billion in 2010. The decrease in research on gas and energy is due to the feasibility of the

</DIV>

increase of 29.1% due to provision for loss of materials, increased distribution of variable
compensation (profit sharing) and review of mining rights.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Result of equity investments</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The equity income result in non-controlled decreased 148.5% from R$ 99&nbsp;million of revenue in 2009

Companhia Sider&#250;rgica do Atl&#226;ntico.

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Net Financial result</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The financial result varied 231.9%, from an income of R$ 2.094&nbsp;billion in 2009 to an expense of R$
2.763&nbsp;billion in 2010. The main factors that contributed to the negative result was the lower
positive monetary and exchange variation recorded in 2009, market marking of shareholders
debentures and expenses with tax on financial operations due to the redemption of securities
convertible into shares.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Gain (loss)&nbsp;on realization of assets</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The gain (loss)&nbsp;on asset realization was of R$ 93&nbsp;million in 2009, mainly due to sale of our sold
the remaining of our stake in Usiminas with a gain of R$ 288&nbsp;million partially offset by a loss in
Valesul of R$ 147&nbsp;million in 2009. In 2010 there have been no gains/losses.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Income taxes</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">For 2010 we recorded a net income tax expense of R$ 7.035&nbsp;billion, compared with R$ 4.954&nbsp;million
in 2009 due to higher tax basis.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Net income</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Net profit increased by 190.9%, from R$ 10.337&nbsp;billion in 2009 to R$ 30.070&nbsp;billion in 2010 is due
primarily to factors explained previously.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Financial year ended December&nbsp;31</B><SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top"><B>st</B></SUP><B>, 2008 compared with the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><B><I>Revenues</I></B>

</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Net operating revenues decreased 31.3% to R$ 48.496&nbsp;billion in 2009 versus R$ 70.541&nbsp;billion in
2008.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">In 2009, the decrease in revenues was determined by lower sales volumes and price decrease of the
main products sold by the Company, contributing for a revenue decrease of R$ 10.919&nbsp;billion and R$
15.876&nbsp;billion, respectively versus 2008.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The contraction in revenues was determined by lower iron ore prices, R$ 4.583&nbsp;billion, and the
decrease in shipments of iron ore, R$ 3.271&nbsp;billion, pellets, R$ 3.545&nbsp;billion, and nickel, R$
1.990&nbsp;billion.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Iron ore</I>
</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Revenues from iron ore sales decreased by 18.9%, from R$ 31.113&nbsp;billion in 2008 to R$ 25.234
billion in 2009, due to a 14.7% drop in the average sale price and a 10.5% fall in sales volumes.
The drop in prices is explained by a decrease in benchmark prices, in U.S. dollars, 28.2% for fines
and 44.5% for lumps. The contraction in global demand for steel, and therefore the decrease in
steel production caused the negative impact in Vale&#146;s sales volumes.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Pellets</I>
</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Revenues from pellet shipments were 60.6% lower, from R$ 9.861&nbsp;billion in 2008 to R$ 3.887&nbsp;billion
in 2009 due to a 27.5% decrease in average sales prices and a 36.1% reduction of sales volumes. The
drop
</DIV>

</DIV>

</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Manganese ore</I>
</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Revenues from manganese ore decreased 39.4%, from de R$ 454&nbsp;million in 2008 to R$ 275&nbsp;million in
2009 due to lower prices. The effect of lower prices was partially offset by a 30% increase in
volumes sold as a result of strong Chinese demand.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Ferroalloys</I>
</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Revenues from ferroalloys sales decreased 63.3%, from R$ 1.886&nbsp;billion in 2008 to R$ 693&nbsp;million in
2009, due to significant drops in sales volumes, of 36.1%, and average prices, of 36.3% due to
reduced demand.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Nickel and other products</I>
</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Revenues from this segment decreased by 43.3%, from R$ 13.865&nbsp;billion in 2008 to R$ 7.868&nbsp;billion
in 2009, mainly due to the following factors:
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>. Revenues from nickel sales decreased 38.9%, from R$ 10.564&nbsp;billion in 2008 to R$ 6.457
billion in 2009, due to a 24.8% decline in average nickel prices. Nickel sales volume declined by
18.8% in 2009 due to the temporary interruption of our Sudbury and Voisey Bay operations as a
result of labor strikes beginning in the second half of 2009; and</I>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>. Revenues from copper sales decreased by 55.4%, from R$ 2.023&nbsp;billion in 2008 to R$ 903
million in 2009, primarily due to a 52.7% drop in volume sold due to the strikes described above.</I>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Copper concentrate</I>
</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Revenues from sales of copper concentrate decreased by 15.6%, from R$ 1.574&nbsp;billion in 2008 to R$
1.329&nbsp;billion in 2009, due to a 17.0% decrease in the average sale price and 5.2% decrease in
volume sold, both impacted by the contraction of the global economy.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Aluminum</I>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Revenues from our aluminum business decreased 27.8%, from R$ 5.843&nbsp;billion in 2008 to R$ 4.217
billion in 2009. The reduction of 33.4% in average prices was mainly responsible for lower revenue.
The variation in average prices is justified by the conditions of world economy.</I>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Potash</I>
</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Revenues from sales of potash increased by 60.1%, from R$ 506&nbsp;million in 2008 to R$ 810&nbsp;million in
2009. The increase was due to a 58.7% increase in volume sold as a result of the strong performance
of the Brazilian agricultural sector. Average prices of potassium remained stable during the
period.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Logistics services</I>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Revenues from logistics services decreased by 22.6%, from R$ 3.666&nbsp;billion in 2008 to R$ 2.838
billion in 2009, due to a sharp fall in the volume of steel inputs transported, as a result of
lower Brazilian exports.</I>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Other products and services</I>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Revenues from other products and services fell from R$ 3.112&nbsp;billion in 2008 to R$ 2.193
billion in 2009 as a result of a reduction in revenues from steel products, decreased 59.5% from R$
1.348&nbsp;billion in 2008 to R$ 546&nbsp;million in 2009, due to the effect of global recession on
activities of steel industry in Brazil.</I>
</DIV>

<DIV style="font-family: Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif">
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Products and Services Costs and Expenses
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Costs related to services and goods sold by Vale are detailed below:
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Comments on Cost by Type of Product
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Our total cost of goods sold decreased from R$ 32.156&nbsp;billion in 2008 to R$ 27.750&nbsp;billion in 2009,
a 13.8% reduction, due to a reduction in volumes sold. The following were the main factors that
contributed to this reduction:
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Outsourced services. Outsourced services costs decreased by 14.8% in 2009, from R$ 5.021
billion in 2008 to R$ 4.276&nbsp;billion in 2009, due to lower volumes sold.</I>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Material costs. Material costs decreased by 9.6% in 2009, from R$ 6.576&nbsp;billion in 2008 to R$
5.943&nbsp;billion in 2009, reflecting a reduction in demand, which was partially offset by increased
maintenance expenses due to preparation for the resumption of operations that were paralyzed.</I>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Energy costs. Energy costs decreased by 21.9% in 2009, from R$ 5.813&nbsp;billion in 2008 to R$
4.537&nbsp;billion in 2009. This reduction reflected lower volumes sold and lower average prices.</I>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Staff costs. Staff costs decreased by 2.8%, from R$ 4.193&nbsp;billion in 2008 to R$ 4.077&nbsp;billion
in 2009, mainly due to lower production levels in response to weaker demand reflecting the
temporary interruption of some mines and plants.</I>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Acquisition of products. Costs related to the acquisition of products from third parties
decreased by 56.7%, from R$ 2.805&nbsp;billion in 2008 to R$ 1.219&nbsp;billion in 2009, driven by lower
volumes of products purchased.</I>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Other costs. These remained relatively steady, going from R$ 7.749&nbsp;billion to R$ 7.698&nbsp;billion
in 2009.</I>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Selling and administrative expenses</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Selling, and administrative expenses decreased by 34.5%, from R$ 3.618&nbsp;billion in 2008 to R$ 2.347
billion in 2009. This decrease was mainly attributable to an adjustment of R$ 748&nbsp;million related
to copper sales that arose from the effects of an adjustment in copper prices under the Month After
Month of Arrival (MAMA)&nbsp;pricing system. Under this pricing system, sales of copper concentrates and
anodes are provisionally priced at the time of shipment, and final prices are settled on the basis
of the LME price for a future period, generally one to three months after the shipment date. In
addition, there was a reduction of expenses in advertising and brand management and personnel
related to new level of product commercialization.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Research and development expenses</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Research and development expenses remained relatively stable, from R$ 2.071&nbsp;billion in 2008 to R$
1.964&nbsp;billion in 2009. The reduction in copper, nickel, coal and logistics research expenses was
compensated by an increase in research related to gas and energy.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Impairment of goodwill</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">No impairment was registered in 2009. In 2008, we recognized R$ 2.447&nbsp;billion impairment of
goodwill associated with our 2006 acquisition of Vale Canada due to the non-recoverability.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Other operating expenses/revenues</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Other operating expenses increased by R$ 2.849&nbsp;billion in 2008 to R$ 3.262&nbsp;billion in 2009, an
increase of 14.4% in consequence of the expense aroused from the interruption of some mines and
plants due to reduced global demand and of the strike in two nickel operations in Canada. In 2008,
other operating expenses were impacted by some non-recurring items: R$ 286&nbsp;million, relating to the
payment of use of rail services by our iron ore operations in the past; R$ 407&nbsp;million, as
provision for loss with materials; and R$ 334&nbsp;million, relating to the provision for losses related
to performance of product inventory.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Income from shareholdings decreased 4.8%, from R$ 104&nbsp;million in 2008 to R$ 99&nbsp;million in 2009.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Financial result</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The financial result varied 154.6%, from an expense of R$ 3.838&nbsp;billion in 2008 to an income of R$
2.094&nbsp;billion in 2009. The main factors that contributed to the positive result were the profits
from derivatives recorded in 2009, due to <I>swaps </I>of real-denominated debt into
U.S. dollars and appreciation of real against U.S. dollar by 25.5% in 2009. In 2008 the loss with
derivatives was due to depreciation of U.S. dollar against the real of 31.9%, due to
similar swap transaction.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Gains (losses)&nbsp;on realization of assets</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The gain (loss)&nbsp;on realization of assets showed a variation of 33.1%, from R$ 139&nbsp;million in 2008
to R$ 93&nbsp;million in 2009, mainly due to sale of our stake in Jubilee Mines in 2008, while in 2009
we sold the remaining of our stake in Usiminas with a gain of R$ 288&nbsp;million partially offset by a
loss in Valesul of R$ 147&nbsp;million.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Income tax</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">For 2009 we recorded a net income tax expense of R$ 4.954&nbsp;billion, compared with R$ 665&nbsp;million in
2008 due to higher tax basis.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Net income</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Net profit reduction by 51.4%, from R$ 21.279&nbsp;billion in 2008 to R$ 10.337&nbsp;billion in 2009 is due
primarily to factors explained previously.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>Position on December&nbsp;31</B><SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top"><B>st</B></SUP><B>, 2009 compared with the position at December&nbsp;31</B><SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top"><B>st</B></SUP><B>,
2009</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Vale has assets and debts referenced to different currencies, the main ones being the real, U.S.
dollar and Canadian dollar. On December&nbsp;31<SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">st</SUP> , 2009, we had 57% of our assets related to
Brazilian reais, 14% to U.S. dollars, 25% to Canadian dollars and 4% to other currencies, while the
majority of our debt was expressed in U.S. dollars. Consequently, the effects of changes in
exchange rates impact the financial statements, especially the U.S. dollar, which in 2009 devalued
4.3% against the real.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Current assets</I></B>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><I>Cash and cash equivalents.</I>

</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The increase of 1.9% from R$ 13.221&nbsp;billion on December&nbsp;31<SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">st</SUP>, 2009, to R$ 13.469&nbsp;billion
on December&nbsp;31<SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">st</SUP>, 2010. Although the company has made funding during 2010 that amounted
to R$ 4.771&nbsp;billion, significant disbursements were made to face loans liquidation, including
debentures due in 2010, and to investments in structure as well as companies acquisitions.

compared to R$ 95.758&nbsp;billion on December&nbsp;31, 2009. The increase in profit reserves of R$ 6.876
billion came from net income capitalization and fundraising with the operation of debt convertible
into shares, in part offset by the cumulative adjustment of conversion basically stemming from
exchange variation of investments.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>10.2) Operating and Financial Results</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><B>a) Results of Vale Operations, in particular:</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><B><I>i. Description of key components of revenue</I></B>
</DIV>




<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->&nbsp;<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Net operating revenues totaled R$ 83.225&nbsp;billion in 2010, increasing 71.4% compared to 2009.
Compared to 2009, net operating revenue decreased 31.5% compared to 2008, when amounted R$ 48.496
billion.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Individually, the most important products in terms of revenue generation (i)&nbsp;in 2010, 2009 and 2008
were: iron ore, nickel, pellets and copper:

<H5 align="left" style="page-break-before:always"><A HREF="#H04912tocpage">Table of Contents</A></H5><P>

<DIV style="font-family: Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif">

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Iron ore and pellets</I>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The demand for iron ore and pellets is a result of the global demand for high carbon steel. The
demand for high carbon steel, in turn, is highly influenced by global industrial production. There
are several quality levels of iron ore and pellets, as well as, several physical characteristics.
Several factors affect the prices of different types of iron ore, such as the iron content of
specific ore deposits, the size of particles, the humidity content and the type and concentration
of contaminants (such as phosphorus, alumina and manganese) in the ore. Generally, the
classification of ore into thin ore, lump ore and pellet feed determines price differences.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Since April&nbsp;2010, all of our iron ore clients have agreed to move from annual reference contracts
to index-based contracts. The former benchmark pricing system was replaced by a new system, as
agreed with our clients, which determines a quarterly price for the iron ore, based on the
three-month average of the index prices for the period ended a month before the start of the new
quarter. Our average prices for iron ore in 2010 increased by 84.9%, and our pellet prices were
118.7% higher than in 2009.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Chinese iron ore imports reached 619.1&nbsp;million metric tons in 2010, just under the 627.8&nbsp;million
metric tons in 2009 and 39.4% above the 2008 level, mainly due to the strong increase in the
Chinese steel production in 2010.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">We expect China&#146;s growth to remain above 10% in the first semester of 2011, driven mainly by
internal demand, and to decrease slightly in the second semester. The demand for minerals and
metals is expected to remain high, not only due to the rapid economic growth, but also due to
restocking.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<B><I>Manganese and ferroalloys</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The prices of manganese ore and ferroalloys are influenced by trends in the high carbon steel
market. The prices of ferroalloys are also influenced by the prices of its main inputs, such as
manganese ore, energy and coke. Manganese ore negotiations are based on the spot market or
calculated on a quarterly basis. Ferroalloys prices are determined on a quarterly basis.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<B><I>Coal</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The demand for metal coal is driven by the demand for steel, especially in Asia. The demand for
thermal coal is directly related to electrical energy consumption, which will continue to be driven
by the worldwide economic growth, especially in emerging economies. Since April&nbsp;2010, the prices of
metallurgical coal are set on a quarterly basis for most volumes sold in the transoceanic market.
The prices of thermal coal are set in spot negotiations and/or through annual contracts.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<B><I>Nickel</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Nickel is traded in the London Metal Exchange (LME). It is mainly used to produce stainless steel,
corresponding on average to 64% of global nickel consumption. Most nickel products are priced
according to a discount or a premium to the LME price, depending on the technical and physical
characteristics of the nickel product. Nickel demand, from sources other than stainless steel
production, represents 36% of the global nickel demand.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">We have short-term fixed-volume contracts with customers for the majority of our expected annual
nickel sales. These contracts, together with our sales for non-stainless steel applications (high
nickel alloys, steel alloys, forging, plating, batteries and special applications), provide stable
demand for a significant portion of our annual production. In 2010, 65% of our refined nickel sales
were destined to applications outside the stainless steel industry. This, when compared to the
industry average of 36% among nickel producers, renders our sales volume more steady. As a result
of our focus on such higher-value segments, our average realized nickel prices have typically
exceeded LME prices.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Primary nickel (including iron-nickel, pig iron and nickel cathode) and secondary nickel (scrap)
are competing sources of nickel for stainless steel production. The choice between the different
types of primary and secondary nickel is largely driven by its relative prices and availability.
Over the past years, secondary nickel accounted for about 42-49% of the overall nickel used in
stainless steel production, and primary nickel accounted for 51-58%. In 2010, the Chinese nickel
pig iron production and iron-nickel production is estimated to have been higher than 150,000 metric
tons, representing 11% of the global offer of primary nickel, compared to 7% in 2009.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Nickel&#146;s foundations are expected to remain strong in the near future. Stainless steel consumption
is strongly correlated with consumer spending and oscillation in relation to income growth. This
helps explaining why nickel consumption rates, measured as consumption per US$ from the GDP, is
still lower in emerging economies than in more advanced economies; unlike other metals, such as
steel and copper. We expect emerging economies to keep the momentum of rapid increase in individual
income, as in previous years, leading the expansion of consumer spending worldwide; this implies
significant growth potential for nickel demand in the medium term.
</DIV>




<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->&nbsp;<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>

<P><HR noshade><P>
<H5 align="left" style="page-break-before:always"><A HREF="#H04912tocpage">Table of Contents</A></H5><P>

<DIV style="font-family: Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif">




<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<B><I>Aluminum</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">In February&nbsp;2011, we transferred part of our aluminum businesses to Norsk Hydro ASA (Hydro), a
large aluminum producer, and we now own 22% of Hydro&#146;s capital. Before this transaction, the
prices of our aluminum were based on the LME prices for the month prior to the sale. Our alumina
prices used to be calculated based on a percentage of the LME aluminum prices; and our bauxite
prices used to be determined by a formula linked to the price of aluminum for three-month futures
contracts on the LME and to the price of alumina FOB Australia.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<B><I>Copper</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Growth in copper demand in recent years has been driven primarily by Chinese imports. Copper prices
are determined on the basis of: (i)&nbsp;copper metal prices on end markets, such as the LME and the
NYMEX; and (ii)&nbsp;for intermediate products, such as cooper concentrate and copper anode (which
represent the majority of our sales), treatment and refining are negotiated with each client.
According to a pricing system known as MAMA (month after month of arrival), sale prices of copper
concentrate and anode are provisionally set at the time of shipment, and the final prices are based
on the LME at a future time, typically three months after shipment.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Copper consumption is rapidly increasing, partly as a result of further recovery in the global
economy. Due to structural limitations to the growth of the supply of concentrates, there are
strong factors driving relatively high prices.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<B><I>Fertilizer nutrients</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The demand for fertilizers is driven by agricultural production, which is dependent on the demand
for food. The latter, in turn, is driven mainly by population increase, age distribution, economic
development and food preferences. The demand may also be driven by biofuel production, which is
determined by economic growth, competition with fossil fuels and environmental regulations.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Fertilizers are sold mainly on a cash-basis, based on international reference prices; although
certain large importers, such as China and India, often sign annual contracts. Seasonality is an
important price driver throughout the year, as agricultural production is dependent on the weather
conditions for each region.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<B><I>Logistics</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Demand for our transportation services in Brazil is primarily driven by Brazilian economic growth,
mainly in the agricultural and steel sectors. Our logistics revenues are primarily from fees
charged to customers for the transportation of cargo on Vale&#146;s railroads, ports and ships. Our
railroads account for most of this revenue. Nearly all of our logistics revenues are expressed in
Brazilian Reais and subject to adjustments triggered by changes in fuel prices. Prices in the
Brazilian market for railroad services are subject to ceilings set by the Brazilian regulatory
authorities, but they primarily reflect competition with the trucking industry.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<B><I>Exchange Rate</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The impact of exchange rate variations on our results are described in item &#147;10.2 (b)&#148;.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>b. Variations of incomes attributable to changes in prices, exchange rates, inflation, changes in
volumes and the introduction of new products and services</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><B><I>Exchange rate variations</I></B>

</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The increase in the value of the US dollar in relation to the Brazilian Real tends to result in
higher operating margins and lower financial results. This is due to exchange gains on our
liabilities in US dollars and fair market value gains on our currency derivatives.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Most of our revenues are expressed in US dollars, whereas most of our costs of goods sold are
expressed in other currencies, mainly the Brazilian Real (69% in 2010), as well as, the US dollar
(15% in 2010). As a result, changes in exchange rates affect our operating margins.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Most of our long-term debt is expressed in US dollars. Due to the fact that Vale&#146;s functional
currency is the Brazilian Real, changes in the value of the US dollar against the Brazilian real
result in exchange gains or losses on our net liabilities, which, in turn, affect our financial
results.
</DIV>




<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->&nbsp;<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">On December&nbsp;31<SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">st</SUP>, 2010 our debt expressed in Brazilian Reais was R$ 13.3&nbsp;billion. Since
most of our revenue is in US dollars, we use derivatives to convert our debt from Brazilian Reais
to US dollars. As a consequence of the depreciation of the Brazilian Real in the first semester,
and its subsequent half, the net exchange rate and monetary variation caused a positive impact on
our net profits of R$ 463&nbsp;million in 2010. The net result of the currency and interest rate swaps,
structured mainly to convert the debt expressed in Brazilian Reis into US dollars to protect our
cash flow from currency price volatility, produced a positive effect of R$ 1.290&nbsp;billion in 2010,
of which R$ 2.240&nbsp;billion generated a positive impact on the cash flow.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Variations in the rates of inflation</I>
</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Our revenues are not significantly affected by inflation rates.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B><I>Variations attributable to price changes, volume changes and the introduction of new products and
services</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Our operating revenue is directly affected by changes to our products&#146; prices and services, as well
as, by changes to the volumes sold, as discussed in item &#147;10.2(a)(ii)&#148; of this Reference Form.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Fertilizers</I>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The fertilizers segment is accountable for the following effects on our results: contribution of R$
3.014&nbsp;billion to our net income in 2010 and of R$ 2.729&nbsp;billion to our costs. The remaining
operations did not have relevant impacts on the Company&#146;s results.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><B>c. Impact of inflation, price variations of main inputs and products, exchange rate and interest
rates on operating results and the issuer&#146;s financial result</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">For comments on the impact of inflation, price variations of main products and exchange rates, see
item &#147;10.2 (b)&#148; of this Reference Form.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">We are exposed to the risk of interest rates for loans and financings. Debt tied to interest rates
in US$ consists mainly of loans, including export prepayment operations, loans from commercial
banks and multilateral organizations. In general, these debts are indexed to the LIBOR (London
Interbank Offered Rate). The natural hedge between North American interest rate fluctuations and
prices of metals mitigates the volatility of Vale&#146;s cash flow. In the event of an imbalance in this
natural hedge, Vale assesses the possibility of contracting financial instruments to provide the
desired protection. The floating rate of our debt expressed in Brazilian Reais includes debentures,
loans obtained from the BNDES, fixed assets and financing for the purchase of services in the
Brazilian market. The interest on these obligations is tied primarily to CDI (Interbank Deposit
certificate), the reference interest rate on the Brazilian interbank market and the TJLP (long-term
interest rate). About 30% of the debt is expressed in Brazilian Reais and is linked to a floating
interest rate; the remaining 70% is expressed in other currencies.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Energy costs are an important component of our production cost and represent 17.4% of the total
cost of products sold in 2010. Increases in the price of oil and gas negatively impact our
logistics, mining, pellets, and nickel and alumina businesses. Electricity costs represented 6.7%
of the total cost of products sold in 2010.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>10.3 Relevant effects on Financial Statements</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The purchase of Vale Fosfatados and Vale Fertilizantes has had significant impacts on our results:
contribution of R$ 3.014&nbsp;billion to our net income in 2010 and of R$ 2.729&nbsp;billion to our costs.
The remaining operations did not have relevant impacts on the Company&#146;s results.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Vale does not provide advisory forecasts regarding its future financial performance. The company
seeks to disclose as much information as possible about its views on the different markets where it
operates, its strategic guidelines and implementation in order to give participants in the capital
market a sound basis for their expectations regarding its performance in the medium and long term.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<B>a. introduction or disposal of operating segment</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">In 2010, the fertilizer segment was introduced and its contribution to the revenue was of 3.8%.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<B>b. incorporation, acquisition or divestiture of equities</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<B><I>Events following the Accounting Statements from the 31</I></B><SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top"><B><I>st</I></B></SUP> <B><I>of December, 2010</I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The following events have not had significant impacts on Vale&#146;s financial statements or its results
in 2010.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><I>Acquisition of Biopalma</I>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">In February&nbsp;2011, Vale became the controller of Biopalma da Amaz&#244;nia S.A. Reflorestamento
Ind&#250;stria e Com&#233;rcio, in Par&#225;, a producer of palm oil, which is used in biodiesel production. The
transaction value was R$ 173.5&nbsp;million. Our goal is to use this fuel in Vale&#146;s operations in
Brazil. Biopalma begins palm oil production in 2011, expecting to reach annual production of
500.000 tons by 2019, when crops reach maturity. The main use of the oil shall be on Vale&#146;s
biodiesel production to fuel its locomotives, machines and equipment in large Brazilian operations,
using the B20 (mixture containing 20% biodiesel and 80% common diesel).
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><I>Portfolio management</I>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">In February&nbsp;2011, Vale announced completion of its transaction with Norsk Hydro ASA (Hydro), a
company listed in the Oslo Stock Exchange and in the London Stock Exchange (ticker symbol: NHY), to
transfer all of its shares with Albras &#151; Alum&#237;nio Brasileiro S.A. (Albras), Alunorte &#151; Alumina do
Norte do Brasil S.A. (Alunorte) and Companhia de Alumina do Par&#225; (CAP), as well as, respective
exclusivity rights, business contracts and net debt of US $655&nbsp;million; in exchange for 22% of
Hydro&#146;s outstanding common shares, following today&#146;s issuance, and US $503&nbsp;million in cash,
following adjustments.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Additionally, Vale has incorporated a new company, namely Paragominas S.A. (Paragominas), and
transferred the Paragominas bauxite mine and all of its remaining bauxite mining rights in Brazil.
As part of this transaction, Vale has sold 60% of Paragominas to Hydro for US $578&nbsp;million in cash,
after working capital adjustments. The remaining 40% shall be sold in two equal shares of 20% in
2013 and 2015, for US $200&nbsp;million in cash each.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Under the terms of the agreement, Vale, through its fully owned subsidiaries, has transferred to
Hydro: (a)&nbsp;51% of the total capital of Albras; (b)&nbsp;57% of the total capital of Alunorte; (c)&nbsp;61% of
the total capital of CAP; and will sell (d)&nbsp;60% of the total capital of Paragominas &#151; Vale will
hold 40% of the capital until it is completely sold in 2015.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Vale, through its fully owned subsidiaries, has subscribed 447,834,465 Hydro shares, or 22% of the
2,035,611,206 outstanding shares, approximately US $3.5&nbsp;billion according to Hydro&#146;s closing price
and the exchange rate NOK/US$ on the 25th of February, 2011. Under the terms of the transaction,
Vale shall not sell its shares for a 2-year lock-up period and shall not own more than the 22% of
Hydro.
</DIV>

</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><I>Acquisition of iron ore assets in Africa</I>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">In April&nbsp;2010, Vale acquired from BSG Resources Ltd. (BSGR)&nbsp;51% equity in BSG Resources (Guinea)
Ltd., which holds concessions for iron ore in Guinea, Simandou South (Zogota) and exploration
permits for Simandou North (Blocks 1 &#038; 2). Vale has paid US $2.5&nbsp;billion for the acquisition of
these assets &#151; US $500&nbsp;million in cash and the remaining US $2&nbsp;billion in installments subject to
the fulfillment of specific goals. Simandou Blocks 1 &#038; 2 are among the best unexploited iron ore
deposits in the world, with high quality and potential for the development of large scale and long
term projects, at low operating and investment costs. The joint venture between Vale and BSGR will
implement the Zogota project and conduct feasibility studies for Blocks 1 &#038; 2, with the creation of
a logistics corridor for the flow of materials through Liberia. For the right to move goods through
Liberia, the joint venture is committed to renewing 660 km of the Trans- Guinea railway for
passenger and light cargo. Vale will be responsible for asset management, marketing and sales of
the joint venture with the exclusive off-take of the iron ore produced.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><I>Acquisition of coal assets in Australia</I>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">In June&nbsp;2010, Vale acquired from AMCI Investments Pty Ltd (AMCI), for US $92&nbsp;million, additional
holdings of 24.5% in the Belvedere coal project. As a result of this transaction, Vale&#146;s
participation in Belvedere increased from 51.0% to 75.5%. Belvedere is an underground coal mine
project in the Bowen Basin region, near the town of Moura in Queensland, Australia. According to
our preliminary estimates, when completed the Belvedere project will have the potential to reach
production capacity of up to 7.0&nbsp;million metric tons of metallurgical coal per year.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><I>Acquisition of assets of fertilizer</I>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In line with our strategy of becoming global leaders in the fertilizer industry, in May&nbsp;2010
we acquired 58.6% of the capital of Fertilizantes Fosfatados S.A. (Fosfertil), currently Vale
Fertilizantes S.A.; as well as, the Brazilian fertilizer assets of Bunge Participa&#231;&#245;es e
Investimentos S.A. (BPI), currently Vale fosfatados, for R$ 8.692&nbsp;billion (corresponding to a price
per share of US $12.0185 for Fosfertil shares and a total of US $1.7&nbsp;billion for Bunge fertilizer
assets). A payment of R$ 103&nbsp;million was made in July to complement the price of Vale Fosfatados.
In September, we acquired a further 20.27% of Fosfertil&#146;s equity for R$ 1.762&nbsp;billion
(corresponding to a price per share of US $12.0185) and, in December, we disclosed the result of
the public offering for the acquisition of the company&#146;s common shares held by minority
shareholders. In December&nbsp;2010, we held 78.92% of the total capital and 99.83% of the voting
capital of Vale Fertilizantes, and 100% of the capital of Vale Fosfatados.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><I>Acquisition of equity on SDCN</I>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In September&nbsp;2010, we acquired 51% of the Sociedade de Desenvolvimento do Corredor Norte S.A.
(SDCN)&nbsp;for R$ 36.615&nbsp;million. SDCN has a concession to create the necessary logistics
infrastructure to enable the flow of the production from the second phase of the Moatize coal

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Iron ore assets in Corumb&#225;</I>
</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">In September&nbsp;2009, Vale concluded the acquisition of the open pit iron ore mining exploration
operations in Corumb&#225;, Brazil, along with its respective logistics infrastructure for US $750
million (equivalent to R$ 1.473&nbsp;billion on the date of disbursement) from Rio Tinto Plc. The
Corumb&#225; iron ore mine is a world class asset, defined by its high iron content, with lump reserves.
The logistics assets support 70% of the operation&#146;s transport needs. The purchase of the Corumb&#225;
assets is subject to Federal Government approval.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Potash deposits in Argentina and Canada</I>
</DIV>
<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">In January&nbsp;2009, Vale purchased the Rio Colorado project from Rio Tinto Plc, in the Mendoza and
Neuqu&#233;n provinces, in Argentina, and the Regina project in the Saskatchewan province, in Canada,
for US $850&nbsp;million (equivalent to R$ 1.995&nbsp;billion on the date of disbursement). The Rio Colorado
project includes the development of a mine with initial rated capacity of 2.4 Mtpy of potash, with
potential for expansion up to 4.35 Mtpy. The project also includes 350 km of railway connections,
port facilities and a power plant. The Regina project is still in its exploration phase, with
potential for annual production of approximately 2.8 Mt of potash. The current local infrastructure
will enable the final product to be transported to Vancouver, facilitating access to the expanding
markets in Asia.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<I>Copper exploitation assets in the African copper belt</I>

Minerals Limited, for future development of TEAL Exploration &#038; Mining Incorporated (TEAL)&nbsp;assets,
for US $60&nbsp;million (equivalent to R$ 139&nbsp;million on the date of disbursement); thus, expanding the
strategic options for growth in the African copper market.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">TEAL has two copper projects in the African copper belt already at feasibility and approval stage.
Over the next few years, these projects together may represent a nominal production capacity of
65,000 metric tons of copper per year, as well as, an extensive and highly promising portfolio of
copper exploitation assets.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><B>10.4 Changes in Accounting Practices. Corrections and Remarks.</B>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<B>a. significant changes in accounting practices</B></DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">There have been no significant changes in the consolidated financial statements for the year ending
on December&nbsp;31<SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">st</SUP> , 2010 except for those relating to the first annual consolidated
financial statements in accordance with the Accounting Pronouncements Committee (CPC)&nbsp;and the
IFRSs. The Company applied the CPC Pronouncements 37 and 43 and IFRS 1 in preparing these
consolidated financial statements. For more details, see Note 5 in the accounting statements.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The individual financial statements of the Parent Company for the year ending on December
31<SUP style="FONT-size: 85%; vertical-align: text-top">st</SUP>, 2010 are the first annual individual demonstrations in accordance with the CPC.
The Company applied CPCs 37 and 43 when preparing these individual financial statements.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The transition date is January&nbsp;1, 2009. The administration prepared balance sheets in accordance
with the CPCs and the IFRS at that date.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">In preparing those financial statements, the Company applied the all relevant mandatory exceptions
and certain optional exemptions regarding the full retrospective application.

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>10.5 Critical Accounting Policies</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The criteria listed below refer to the critical accounting policies that are adopted and reflected
in the consolidated financial statements.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">We considered an accounting policy critical when it is important to the financial condition and
operations results and requires significant judgments and estimates by the Vale management. The
summary of most important accounting policies can be found in Note 3 of the financial statements.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The presentation of financial statements in accordance with the principles of recognition and
measurement by the accounting standards issued by the CPC and the IASB requires the Company
management to make judgments, estimates and assumptions that may affect the value of assets and
liabilities presented.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">These estimates are based on the best information available in each period and the actions planned
and are constantly reviewed based on available information. Changes in facts and circumstances may
lead to revision of estimates, so the actual future results could differ from estimates.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Significant estimates and assumptions used by management in preparing these financial statements
are thus presented:
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><I>Mineral reserves and mine life</I>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The estimates of proven reserves and probable reserves are regularly evaluated and updated. Proven
and probable reserves are determined using techniques generally accepted geological estimates. The
calculation of reserves requires the Company to assume positions of future conditions that are
uncertain, including future ore prices, exchange rates, inflation rates, mining technology,
availability of permits and production costs. Changes in some of these assumptions could have a
significant impact on proven reserves and probable reserves recorded.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The estimated volume of mineral reserves is based on calculation of the exhaust portion of the
mines, and the estimated mine life is a major factor in quantifying the provision of environmental
rehabilitation of mines during the write-down of fixed assets. Any change in the estimates of the
volume of mine reserves and life of assets linked to them may have significant impact on charges
for depreciation, depletion and amortization recognized in financial statements as cost of goods
sold. Changes in estimated mine life could cause significant impact on estimates of the provision
for environmental costs of recovery after write-down of fixed assets and impairment analysis<I>.</I>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><I>Environmental costs and recuperation of areas degraded</I>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Expenses related to compliance with environmental regulations are recorded in income or are
capitalized. These programs were designed to minimize the environmental impact of activities.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The Company recognizes an obligation under the market value for disposal of assets during the
period in which they occur, according to Note 2 (s)&nbsp;in the financial statements.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The Company believes the accounting estimates related to reclamation and closure costs of a mine
are a critical accounting policy because it involves significant values for the provision and it
is expected to involve several assumptions, such as interest rate, inflation, life the asset,
considering the current stage of exhaustion and the projected date of exhaustion of each mine.
Although the estimates are revised each year, this provision requires that the premises are assumed
to project cash flows applicable to the operations.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><I>Income tax and social contribution</I>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The determination of the provision for income taxes or deferred income tax assets and liabilities
and any valuation allowance on tax credits requires estimates from Management. For each income tax
asset, the Company assesses the likelihood of part or the entire asset not being recovered. The
valuation allowance made with respect to accumulated tax losses depends on the assessment by the
Company, the probability of generating future taxable profits in the deferred income tax asset was
recognized based on production and sales planning, commodity prices, costs of operational plans,
restructuring costs, reclamation costs and planned capital.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The Company recognizes, where applicable, provision for losses in cases where tax credits may not
be fully recoverable in the future.
</DIV>


<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->&nbsp;<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>

<!-- PAGEBREAK -->
<P><HR noshade><P>
<H5 align="left" style="page-break-before:always"><A HREF="#H04912tocpage">Table of Contents</A></H5><P>

<DIV style="font-family: Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif">




<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><I>Contingencies</I>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Contingent liabilities are recorded and/or disclosed unless the possibility of loss is considered
remote by our legal advisors. These contingencies are arranged in notes to the financial
statements, Notes 2 (s)&nbsp;and 20 of the financial statements.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The record of the contingencies of a given liability on the date of the financial statements is
done when the value of these losses can be reasonably estimated. By their nature, contingencies
will be resolved when one or more future events occur or fail to occur. Typically, the occurrence
of such events depends not on our performance, which makes it difficult to give precise estimates
about the exact date on which such events are recorded. Assessing such liabilities, particularly in
the uncertain legal environment in Brazil, and in other jurisdictions, involves exercising
significant estimates and judgments from management regarding the results of future events.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><I>Post-retirement benefits for employees</I>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The Company sponsors various plans for post-retirement benefits to employees in Brazil and abroad,
the parent company and entities in the Group, as described in note 2 (t)&nbsp;and 22 of the financial
statements.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The values reported in this section depend on a number of factors that are determined based on
actuarial calculations using several assumptions in order to determine the costs and liabilities,
among others. One of the assumptions used in determining the amounts to be recorded in accounting
is the interest rate to discount and upgrade. Any changes in these assumptions will affect the
accounting records made.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The Company, together with external actuaries, reviews at the end of each fiscal year, which
assumptions should be used for the following year. These premises are used for upgrades and
discounts to fair value of assets and liabilities, costs and expenses and determination of future
values of estimated cash outflows, which are needed to settle the obligations with the plans.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><I>Reduction in recoverable value of assets</I>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The Company annually tests the recoverability of its tangible and intangible assets with indefinite
useful lives that are mostly of the portion of premium for expected future earnings arising from
processes of the business combination. The accounting policy in respect of an item is presented in
Note 2 (n)&nbsp;of the financial statements and the possible values and procedures used for the
calculations and records are presented in Note 18 of the financial statements.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Recoverability of assets based on the criterion of discounted cash flow depends on several
estimates, which are influenced by market conditions prevailing at the time that such impairment is
tested and thus management believes it is not possible to determine whether new impairment losses
will occur in the future.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><I>Fair Value of Derivatives and Other Financial Instruments</I>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The fair value of financial instruments not traded in an active market is determined by using
valuation techniques. Vale uses assessments to choose the various methods and assumptions set which
are mainly based on market conditions existing at balance sheet date, see note 24 in the financial
statements.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">The impact analysis if actual results are different from the management estimate is presented in
note 26 of the financial statements on the topic of sensitivity analysis.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><I>Conversion of foreign currency transactions</I>
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The rights and monetary obligations denominated in foreign currencies are converted at
exchange rates prevailing at the balance sheet date, being US$1.00 is equivalent to R$1.6662
on December&nbsp;31, 2010 (US$1.00 equivalent to R$1.7412 on December&nbsp;31, 2009 and R$2.3370 on
December&nbsp;31, 2008).</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Sales revenues, costs and expenses denominated in foreign currencies are converted
using the average exchange rates for the month of their occurrence.</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 12pt"><B>10.6 Internal Controls</B>
</DIV>


<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt"><!-- Folio -->&nbsp;<!-- /Folio -->
</DIV>

<!-- PAGEBREAK -->
<P><HR noshade><P>

<DIV style="font-family: Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif">




<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt"><B>a. degree of efficiency of such controls, and any imperfections and actions taken to correct them</B>
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Vale management evaluated the effectiveness of internal controls related to financial statements
through a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial
reporting and the preparation of financial statements.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">Management established a process for evaluating internal controls with statistical process mapping
and risk assessment to identify applicable controls in order to mitigate the risks affecting the
company&#146;s ability to start, authorize, record, process and disseminate relevant information in
financial statements.
</DIV>


<DIV align="left" style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt">At the end of fiscal year, based on tests performed by the administration during the period, no
shortcomings were identified in the implementation of relevant controls. During the fiscal year,
whenever inadequacies are identified in the implementation of controls, they are corrected through
the implementation of action plans to ensure their effectiveness at year end.
</DIV>
